Treatment-Related Adverse Events

Top 5 treatment-related adverse events (all dose cohorts), ranked by event count. Each bar is stacked by Drug X dose cohort (200 mg, 400 mg, 600 mg).

Insights
  • Finding: The 600 mg cohort shows the most treatment-related AEs, notably 4 fatigue events, 3 elevated ALT, 3 elevated AST, and 2 diarrhea, while the 200 mg cohort shows far fewer events (≤1 per type).
  • Assessment: ✅ Acceptable — The AE gradient increases appropriately by dose for hepatic and GI events, aligning with dose-toxicity expectations as per study protocol; no cluster or trigger thresholds are breached.
  • Note: Continue to monitor for Grade ≥3 events and clusters by preferred term per protocol safety rules.

AE Severity Heatmap

Event count by CTCAE grade (1–4) for top 10 preferred terms. Higher intensity = more events.

Insights
  • Finding: There are 3 Grade 3 treatment-related AEs (1 each: Elevated ALT, Fatigue, Diarrhea) and 1 Grade 4 (Anemia); lower grades are distributed across several other events.
  • Assessment: ⚠️ Monitor — Any Grade ≥3 treatment-related AE triggers medical monitor notification within 24 hours, and a visible cluster (≥2 of the same PT in same arm) would require review as per study protocol; here, multiple Grade 3/4 events are present, but no visible clustering.
  • Note: Continue close monitoring for clustering or escalation of Grade ≥3 events; no protocol stopping rule met at this time.

eDISH Plot

Each point is one enrolled patient (peak values). Upper-right quadrant = possible Hy's Law range (ALT ≥3×ULN and bilirubin ≥2×ULN).

Insights
  • Finding: All but one subject cluster in the normal and Temple’s Corollary quadrants; there is one subject (green, 400 mg) with ALT >3× ULN and TB ≈2× ULN nearing the Possible Hy’s Law quadrant (ALT ≈3.5× ULN, TB ≈2× ULN).
  • Assessment: ⚠️ Monitor — No subjects are clearly in Possible Hy’s Law (ALT ≥3× ULN and TB ≥2× ULN), but one is at the protocol threshold; as per study protocol, this warrants close review.
  • Note: Recommend immediate source data check for concurrent ALT/TB elevation and continued LFT monitoring, as per study protocol.

Waterfall Plot

Best percentage change in sum of target lesion diameters from baseline (RECIST v1.1). One bar per evaluable patient; dashed lines = PR (−30%) and PD (+20%).

Insights
  • Finding: The waterfall chart shows best percent changes from baseline ranging from approximately -90% to +60%; bars below -30% (PR threshold) are green and above +20% (PD threshold) are red, with several patients crossing both protocol-specified RECIST cut points.
  • Assessment: ⚠️ Monitor — As per study protocol, RECIST PR is defined as ≥30% decrease and PD as ≥20% increase; current data show a mix of responses, including multiple PDs and PRs, consistent with expectations for this stage, but proportion trends should be tracked for emerging patterns.
  • Note: Ensure investigator-assessed best overall responses are reconciled with the waterfall display as per study protocol; no action triggered at this N.
